title: Post-Tribunal reflections: Dagmar's paranoia, Dustin's fame, and a wood sliver from every prize
notes: The table's go-around on how each PC is processing an unplanned #1 finish. Dagmar is deep in a paranoia spiral about what winning "for real" now exposes the covenant to, and starts covertly marking every prize item in case something is swapped or stolen later. Dustin is just thrilled to be famous.
source: Transcript 2026-06-20 — table go-around on 'reflections on last time.'
body_text:
**Dagmar** came out of the Tribunal shell-shocked rather than triumphant — the plan had been to lay low, and instead the covenant is now the most visible independent in Normandy. He's replaying how the lay-low/throw-the-match plans went "horribly, horribly wrong" and is settling into a genuinely paranoid stretch: watching for anyone paying the covenant too much attention, and bracing for **Solving** (his long-vanished parens) to reappear and have opinions about all of it — table joke: "he just went out for milk, he'll be back any day now."
**Concrete paranoia measure:** for every book, scroll, or other prize item the covenant receives from the Tribunal, Dagmar takes a **tiny sliver from it** to keep on his person — insurance so that if something underhanded happens later (a swap, a theft, tampering) he has a physical/arcane link to try to trace it back.
**Dustin**, by contrast, is delighted. He reads the win as unambiguously good for his personal legacy and renown, even if the *kind* of fame it brings (a jumped-up sea-covenant embarrassing three leash covenants at their own tournament) isn't necessarily the flattering kind. Table comparison: reputation as faction-specific currency — Order-of-Hermes fame doesn't automatically convert to goodwill with covenants that just got shown up.

title: Stijntje's first taste of peers — and of how different she is from them
notes: Stijntje's real takeaway from the Tribunal wasn't the tournament — it was meeting other apprentices for the first time and discovering how little she has in common with them beyond the mechanics of being gauntleted.
source: Transcript 2026-06-20 — Dustin's reflection on Stijntje's Tribunal experience.
body_text:
For **Stijntje**, the standout experience of the Tribunal wasn't the tournament at all — it was simply having **peers for the first time**: other apprentices her own age and status, something her isolated upbringing on a ship-based covenant never afforded her.
That contact cut both ways. Meeting them made it obvious how different her situation is: she no longer has to actively pass as male in every context now that other apprentices clock the gender gap in the room; she is visibly **more affluent and educated** than most of the other apprentices, who mostly went straight from whatever village they were discovered in to a stationary covenant; and she has simply **seen more of the world** than any of them, most of whom haven't gone much of anywhere. Table comparison: something like growing up on a cruise ship.
Likely friction: her nobility and evident worldliness read to the other apprentices as gloating even when it isn't meant that way — the classic "you haven't been to Cancún" dynamic, just transposed into Hermetic apprenticeship.
Underscored again in this conversation: she did **run away from home** for reasons still unstated, and back home she has to fight the covenant's pig for bed space — her situation isn't as charmed as the other apprentices might assume from her manner.

title: An old wrinkle resurfaces: one of the covenant's ships was pirated from Scarem Montem
notes: While planning Wilhelm's return trip to Scarem Montem for his stolen manuscript, the table half-remembers that the ship they'd send him on was itself taken from Scarem Montem at some point in the covenant's past. Floated as either a bargaining chip (ship for book) or a very awkward thing to show up in.
source: Transcript 2026-06-20 — 'is that the one we pirated?' aside during travel planning.
body_text:
While discussing how Wilhelm gets back to **Scarem Montem** to retrieve his stolen Latin thesis copy, the table worked out that one of the covenant's own vessels was **originally taken from Scarem Montem** — the exact circumstances weren't nailed down on-mic ("I forgot, is that the one we pirated?"), but the ship's provenance was confirmed.
**Two framings floated, unresolved:** (1) rough justice — "fair's fair," they took the book, the covenant already has the ship; or (2) a literal bargaining chip — offer to return the ship in exchange for the manuscript.
Practical warning: **Wilhelm should not sail into Scarem Montem aboard their own stolen ship** to ask for his book back. One bit of dark comedy floated: Wilhelm doesn't actually know it's a stolen ship, and could plausibly be kept in the dark and told it's "a legally distinct ship, note the different name painted right over the old one."
Open thread: which ship this is, exactly, and whether the swap-for-swap idea gets pitched to Scarem Montem when Wilhelm goes back in 1224.

title: The covenant turns a corner: breakeven, trade economics, and an eye on jurisdictional arbitrage
notes: First real financial good news for the covenant: they broke even last year (not counting loan repayment), and with the Tribunal's hard assets in hand, profitability is now "fairly trivial" if they want it. Extended discussion of the Rule of Silver, magically-produced trade goods, and long-range multi-tribunal trade routes.
source: Transcript 2026-06-20 — extended trade-rules and Rule-of-Silver discussion.
body_text:
**State of the covenant's finances, per the GM:** the covenant **broke even last year** — costs did not exceed revenue, though that figure doesn't yet include any loan repayment. With the Tribunal's prize assets now in hand (on top of the Duke's existing payments), the covenant is past its early hard-scrabble years; **real profitability is now trivial to reach** if the party chooses to prioritize it. Not destitute any longer "unless it is your choice or a great failure."
**The Rule of Silver:** a magus may create at most **2 lbs of silver-value goods per Tribunal per year** without inviting real scrutiny — enforcement varies enormously by Tribunal (some care only if the goods are magical weapons; the Rhine Tribunal cares if magic touched the goods or their transport *at all*). Salt (desalinated seawater, reduced to solid) is the easiest magically-produced trade good; explicitly discussed as "legit trade" even though magically created, so long as it's kept under the radar per-Tribunal.
**Jurisdictional arbitrage:** with ~5-6 Tribunals reasonably reachable by ship (Rhine, Normandy, Stonehenge, Hibernia, plus further effort to reach Novgorod), the covenant could legally clear roughly **60-100 lbs of silver a year** just by distributing sales across multiple Tribunals' individual limits — a genuine, legal income stream, separate from anything shadier.
**Infrastructure idea (not yet committed):** an enchanted **stone cargo-sled** — a two-ton, four-ton-loaded flying platform, ~Level 20 enchantment, ~45 mph, functionally a magical helicopter for hauling trade goods (and echoing the departed PC **Kor Ex Flambeau**'s unfinished, much larger version of the same idea, last seen unfinished somewhere out in the world).
**Attitude check:** the table explicitly flagged that each PC sits differently on a "how much do I care about the rules" scale for magically-tinged trade — Dagmar didn't care until the Tribunal made clear people *will* make an example of the covenant if caught, and has shifted hard toward caution as a result.

title: Éogan buys jade for a future Talisman; Dagmar eyes a longevity ritual; Dustin catches up on his own Arts
notes: Three separate long-horizon character projects declared in the same conversation.
source: Transcript 2026-06-20 — personal-project asides during season planning.
body_text:
**Éogan** picked up **jade** (preferred over plain crystal — house-ruled as +Aquam) at the Tribunal markets, with an eye toward beginning work on a **Talisman** — his reasoning: a magus doesn't need to be especially powerful to start one, and the earlier it's begun the more useful it becomes over time.
**Dagmar** is starting to plan toward a **longevity ritual**, aware the covenant's magi are getting into their late twenties. He's deliberately **not** rushing it — real aging doesn't set in until around 35, and he wants his **Creo** significantly stronger before he attempts the ritual, so he's treating this as prep work for "next year or so" rather than an immediate project. (Noted in passing: longevity rituals also cause infertility — a real cost, not just a delay.)
**Dustin** admits to having **neglected his own Arts study** recently between running trade and teaching Stijntje, and is planning to make time to catch up on both fronts going forward.

title: Éogan's Connacht backstory, laid bare
notes: In the course of planning the Ireland trip, Éogan's player laid out his full backstory for the first time: a hedge-magic hostage exchange, an ex-Miscellanea dowsing parens, and a covenant called Vigil at the top of the map.
source: Transcript 2026-06-20 — Éogan's backstory laid out during Hibernia map planning.
body_text:
Éogan is originally from **Connacht** (heard on tape as "conduct") — the region of Ireland the transcript describes as *not* under Hermetic control, where hedge magi "made their last stand." A standing treaty between the Hibernia Tribunal and Connacht's hedge tradition requires Connacht to hand over **seven Gifted individuals per Tribunal cycle**; Éogan was one of the seven traded over as a child.
He was apprenticed not to a hedge magus but to a Hermetic one — **an ex-Miscellanea magus, one of the last of a line of "dowsing wizards"** (the water-finding tradition Éogan referenced back at the Tribunal itself). His upbringing was mostly **wandering between magic sites**, learning directly from the source rather than from formal instruction, with the covenant **Vigil** (marked at the far north of the Hibernia map) as the place he returned to for what formal book-learning he did get.
Practically: this gives the Ireland trip a real anchor — Éogan could write ahead to his old covenant (Vigil) to arrange a night or two of hospitality, or route the party to somewhere closer to the Connacht border and send research assistants in ahead as native-guided scouts.

title: Dagmar's winter at Oleron: the books, the rival-turned-acquaintance, and a crash course in Tribunal politics
notes: With Confluensis having reneged, Oleron becomes the actual custodian of the covenant's tournament-prize books — and Dagmar decides to winter there in person rather than just visiting for a season, for three separate reasons.
source: Transcript 2026-06-20 — Dagmar's season-and-winter plans.
body_text:
The covenant's tournament-prize books and texts are going to **Oleron** — the book-storage question left open when Bertrand ex Verditius denied any arrangement (see the earlier Tribunal-week entries) resolves here, quietly, in Oleron's favor, consistent with how warmly Raoul had already been treating the covenant.
**Dagmar will winter at Oleron in person**, not just spend a working season there, with three stated goals: (1) actually use/study the prize texts on-site, (2) spend time with **the Criamon magus he faced in the Dimicatio final** (Karis, unnamed on this call but clearly the same rival — "he hasn't been with a member of his own order in a very long time"), and (3) get properly briefed on the Tribunal politics the covenant has just stepped into, which he admits he still doesn't fully understand.
His ship will return for him come **spring 1224**.
**Formal follow-up flagged:** since Oleron is now functioning as something like an informal protector/patron without a real vassal agreement (echoing the English Duke/Earl distinction raised at the table), the covenant should send a **formal representative** to Oleron to acknowledge the relationship properly — Dagmar, already headed there, offered the covenant's trade/commerce capacity as a thank-you gesture.

title: Ireland travel plan finalized: Dublin, the coast, and wintering near Carrick
notes: SUPERSEDES the wintering plan in the session-6 'Season plans' entry, which had the covenant wintering on the Isle of Man this year — that's now just a waypoint stop. They winter near Carrick, Ireland instead, buying more research/lab time before sailing home in spring 1224.
source: Transcript 2026-06-20 — Hibernia map/travel planning.
body_text:
**Route, drawn live on the map:** sail to **Dublin**, then follow the Irish coast, then cut inland — with a stop at **Carrick** flagged as a likely landing/basing point.
**Party:** Éogan and Wilhelm are the default travelers; **Dustin** opted in, bringing **Stijntje** and the rest of his entourage.
**Wintering — REVISED.** The original plan (see the session-6 season-planning entry) was to winter on the Isle of Man. That's now just a stop along the way: instead, the party will **winter near Carrick, Ireland**, which buys Wilhelm, Dustin, and Stijntje more time for research and lab activity before departing again in spring. The Isle of Man wintering is deferred to **next year** instead.
**A loose end for later:** the Isle of Man does have an **unclaimed vis source** earmarked as available for Wilhelm's eventual use, once the covenant actually winters there.
**Justifying Wilhelm's continued presence** (an out-of-fiction bookkeeping point the table addressed directly): rather than force an awkward in-fiction reason for a non-covenant-member magus to keep traveling with the party indefinitely, the group leaned on Ars Magica's usual seasonal structure — Wilhelm doesn't need a permanent role, just a standing arrangement (a boat, lab space, an open invitation) that can plausibly explain months or years of divergence and reunion without it being a plot problem.

title: Looking to 1224: back to Scarem Montem, and a still-unfinished prize list
notes: Forward-looking beats confirmed for next year, plus two open threads the GM flagged as still pending on their end.
source: Transcript 2026-06-20 — closing look-ahead to 1224.
body_text:
**1224:** once winter breaks, **Wilhelm heads to Scarem Montem** — "perhaps with some backup" — to retrieve his stolen Latin thesis copy in person.
**Open thread — remaining prize picks.** The GM acknowledged their notes on the covenant's full Tribunal prize list (beyond the Mont-Saint-Michel tide pools, the Terram summa, and Subtle Knives already locked in) were incomplete going into this session and need a second pass before the remaining ~20 prize pawns can be resolved.
**Open thread — vis-source delegation.** With a much larger prize/resource footprint than before, the covenant will need to actively decide who staffs which vis-harvesting season and where — flagged as "too much to think about right now," deferred to once the full resource list is in hand. Noted in passing: harvesting conventions vary by source — some (like Fire From the Sky) require being present for a specific trigger event, others can be left to accumulate and harvested later as needed, Hibernian-hedge-tradition style.

scene: Friday morning — Wilhelm rereads his own thesis
title: Wilhelm's manuscript reveals a Divine-vis wrinkle
notes: Rereading his own folk-magic thesis, Wilhelm clocks that once a magic-theory guideline exists for a phenomenon, its basic lab-activity benefits open up to anyone — including vis harvesting inside holy auras. Which means spells cast with that vis become, technically, Implements of the Divine.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — opening scene, Wilhelm's Creo/Vim magic-theory tangent before the finals.
body_text:
With a day or two of downtime before the last finals, Wilhelm went back over his own manuscript more carefully than he had in weeks.
The catch: per the standard Hermetic rule that developing a magic-theory guideline unlocks the **basic benefits of laboratory activities** for anyone using it, and Wilhelm's folk-magic system covers all four Techniques/Forms-equivalent phenomena — the implication is that mundanes trained through his system could **harvest vis**, including from **holy (Divine) auras**, not merely fae or magical ones.
The wrinkle: magic built from Divine vis apparently becomes, by the working theory at the table, an **Implement of the Divine** — not corrupted or penalized, just now legally/theologically "God's," implicitly, the way a company logo becomes a stakeholder's the moment it appears in a film. No botch penalty attached, but a real second-order consequence for anyone drawing on it.
Wilhelm's gallows-humor read on the Church angle: if anyone in Rome ever actually reads the thesis rather than reacting to rumors of it, their most likely response is a startled, genuine thank-you.

scene: Friday morning — Dietrich holds court in a tavern
title: Dietrich pitches folk magic to scholars and a Redcap; Dustin interrogates him
notes: Wilhelm's brother Dietrich — a Cologne cathedral-school professor with a rhetorician's Presence — works a tavern crowd of mundane scholars and a Redcap. Dustin needles him hard on the Divine-vis danger; Dietrich extends Parma Magica for a proper scholastic debate rather than back down. Éogan and Dagmar eavesdrop with opposite reactions.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — 'the professor' / Dietrich tavern scene and Dustin's cross-examination.
body_text:
**Dietrich** (Wilhelm's brother — professor of medicine and philosophy at a Cologne cathedral school, more at home teaching in a tavern's back room than a formal hall) held forth to a knot of mundane scholars and at least one Redcap, evangelizing his brother's folk-magic thesis.
His pitch, in the confident, theatrical register of a man used to lecturing: mundanes can do "basic magic" once the system is taught — season-long lab work, a few pounds of vis, eventually casting on their own — and the system appears to work equally well in Divine auras ("align your magic with the will of God"), a claim he leans on hard rhetorically.
**Dustin listened in but pushed back sharply**, especially on the vis-from-holy-auras point ("wait, that's dangerous"). Dietrich's answer: no more dangerous than fae vis, just with its own side effects — and he clearly felt Dustin's Gift as an unpleasant edge to the conversation, gritted through it, then formally offered to have **Parma Magica extended** over him so they could debate as scholars instead. Dustin agreed; **no botch** on the roll.
Under structured debate, Dietrich laid out the three ways to learn a new Hermetic guideline — experimentation, being taught via initiation, or **integrating someone else's prior understanding of it** — and used Wilhelm as the live example: Wilhelm was taught actual folk **dowsing/"folk banding"** as a child, before his Gift opened, and that knowledge survived the Opening intact. That's the seed the whole thesis grew from.
The system's theorized reason for being so **syncretic** (working across pagan, fae, and Divine contexts alike): unlike Hermetic magic, it doesn't call on "gods of magic" or power names at all — it calls on **humanity's own innate relationship to nature**. Dietrich's framing: everyone with the Gift has magical "perfect pitch"; this system argues *everyone* — Gifted or not — has *rhythm*. Someone at the table called it a **proto-Spinozist magic system**.
Dietrich also aired the thesis's acknowledged problems: success would mean **thousands of new folk-magic practitioners** wanting into a Rhine/Normandy magical economy sized for a much smaller Order — a real resource and wild-vis strain — plus the obvious Church-scrutiny risk. He name-drops one cautionary case his researchers turned up: someone practicing what looked like infernal magic (commanding reality directly — "you will do this for me") who turned out not to be invoking anything demonic at all, just committing the sin of pride. His answer to Church risk, delivered as pure rhetorical bravado: send *him* their scholars, he'll happily walk them through it.
One concrete new mechanical thread surfaced: folk-magic guidelines can apparently support **spontaneous casting at Boundary and Year durations**, targets/durations normally locked to formal ritual infrastructure. Flagged as something **Valdemar** — already pulling at spontaneous-magic threads — would find very interesting, though he's keeping that interest close to the chest for now.
**Éogan and Dagmar eavesdropped from the side.** Éogan recalled a person or two from his own village who could do small folk-magic-flavored things (calming/calling animals) without ever being identified as Gifted, and mused that formalizing hedge traditions into Hermetic theory could help magi be seen as less of pariahs among mundanes. Dagmar stayed openly unconvinced by the showmanship of the pitch — not the substance, just the hard sell — and was characteristically blunt that he hopes someone else does the actual integration work; his own priority remains keeping the covenant solvent.

scene: Friday morning — Wilhelm and Éogan on sea magic
title: Wilhelm pitches Éogan on hedge-magic sea/weather traditions for the thesis
notes: Wilhelm's working theory is that Hermetic guidelines are mechanically universal, so finding hedge-magic equivalents (storm prediction, current-finding) anywhere would support the thesis. Éogan's own home tradition turns out to be water-finding rather than sea-current work, and runs close to Diedne-adjacent "Seekers" fieldwork methodology.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — Wilhelm/Éogan conversation on weather-working and water traditions.
body_text:
Wilhelm's next concrete step for the thesis: find **weather-prediction or current-navigation** hedge traditions to demonstrate the system generalizes to a sea-faring context, not just land-bound folk practice.
His reasoning (per his working theory that **Hermetic guidelines are effectively universal targets** in game terms): a hedge tradition anywhere that reliably finds ocean currents or predicts storms would independently validate his thesis, regardless of who practices it.
**Éogan's read from experience:** for a sea covenant, control over wind and current isn't just survival — it's propulsion. He's personally more water- than air-inclined. But his own home tradition, as he understands it, wasn't actually a sea-navigation practice — it was oriented toward **finding fresh water inland/underground** for villages, and is more commonly associated with **fae magic** than open-ocean work.
Éogan noted his tradition survived mostly as an unbroken master-to-student thread ("a Hermetic cell in and of itself") rather than a documented body of theory, and that its more active practitioners run in the methodology of House Diedne's **Seekers** suborder — fieldwork his own research assistants use without having formally joined the Seekers themselves.
Open thread: Wilhelm still needs an actual example of hedge-magic sea-current-finding or storm-prediction to close the thesis's weakest citation gap; dowsing-for-water is closer to confirmed but doesn't fully prove the maritime case.

title: Dagmar and Dustin pitch Bertrand ex Verditius on storing the covenant's prizes
notes: With prize books and texts about to become a shipboard liability, Dagmar and Dustin pitch Confluensis (spelled "Confluences" in this session's transcript — same liege covenant as in prior sessions) on custodianship, not vassalage. Bertrand ex Verditius negotiates in person; a Bargain roll closes the terms, contingent on him checking with the covenant's inner circle before the finals end.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — the Confluensis book-storage negotiation with Bertrand.
body_text:
Anticipating a haul of prize books and texts too valuable to risk at sea, Dagmar and Dustin sought out **Confluensis** at their tents to propose safekeeping — explicitly *not* vassalage, just custodianship with guaranteed access.
Met **Bertrand ex Verditius** — visually a man in his 50s who is, in fact, closer to 70 or 80; tanned, Mediterranean coloring; a big, bushy black beard. Bertrand needled Dagmar good-naturedly about a sea-covenant producing "such fine specimens."
**The pitch:** Confluensis holds any prize books/texts on Sjórseiðr's behalf; Sjórseiðr keeps full access and visits to work on them as needed; no formal vassalage, just a standing mutual arrangement.
**Dagmar rolled Area Lore: Normandy Tribunal** (stress die, +3 for prior tribunal research), got an **11**, and learned Confluensis is **significantly underperforming this Tribunal relative to its usual standing** — a covenant that pools and redistributes vassal winnings, meaning a bad Confluensis showing hurts its vassals too, and they're currently short on the usual leverage that comes with hosting a favor like this.
**Payment discussion:** the standard rate for a season of a magus's lab service is roughly **2–3 pawns of vis**. Bertrand fished for what else Sjórseiðr could offer instead — and, after a pointed once-over of Dagmar, asked outright whether **cross-border courier/smuggling work** was something they'd done before. Dagmar demurred; Dustin didn't — the covenant had, in fact, run exactly this kind of job already (the covert Creo Vis run for Montverte, kept off the Redcap network at Montverte's insistence).
**Dustin led the Bargain roll** (Communication, +3 assist from Dagmar) — **no botch**. Closing pitch: a season of general service is fine; being treated as someone's subordinate is not.
Bertrand agreed to take the offer back to Confluensis's inner circle (roughly 10–11 active magi at their home covenant; only a small contingent present at the Tribunal) and promised an answer **before the finals concluded**.

title: Covenant settles on reachable Aquam/Animal vis sources, passes on the Channel Islands claim
notes: Pre-prize-draft strategizing: stick to coastal resources reachable by ship, don't overextend into unfriendly inland territory, and let Confluensis keep its long-disputed Channel Islands claim as a goodwill chip.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — vis-source planning ahead of the prize draft.
body_text:
Before the prize draft, the covenant weighed which vis sources to prioritize if the tribunal went well: **easy access mattered more than the resource type** — trading covers most raw vis needs, but travel through unfriendly or distant territory is a real risk.
GM-offered candidates within easy reach of the covenant's current position: an **Aquam vis source** — sea foam gathered on **St. Martin's Day (November)** at a secluded beach near **Saint-Malo** — and an **Animal vis source** on a cliff along the north shore, near Confluensis's own territory. Both reachable via the English Channel without circling Brittany.
The **Channel Islands vis source** (disputed jurisdiction with the London Tribunal, long held by Confluensis) came up as a possible claim — the covenant chose to **pass on contesting it**, reasoning that Confluensis will simply out-rank them on the pick order anyway, and letting Confluensis keep an already-held resource is a low-cost way to bank goodwill rather than open a jurisdictional fight the covenant doesn't need.

title: Valdemar's joust final vs. Montverte — second place
notes: Valdemar's bracket wins put him in the final against Montverte, tied for the tribunal lead. After debating the politics of beating a host/leash covenant, the table votes to let him go for the win. Montverte takes it fair and square in a best-of-three roll-off.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — joust final roll-off vs. Montverte.
body_text:
Valdemar returned from his bracket having won cleanly against an early opponent and then against a **Semita Errabunda** rider, putting him in the **joust final against Montverte**, tied for first overall.
**Covenant debate:** finishing above a hosting leash-covenant risks the kind of resentment already visible from Confluensis; some at the table favored letting Montverte have it as a courtesy. Consensus landed on **going for the win regardless** — "let the chips fall where they may."
**Best-of-three stress-die roll-off.** Montverte took it **2–1**, fair and square.
Table joked about whether the loss was secretly thrown; consensus in-fiction was no — **Valdemar is confident enough to have pulled it off, but too prideful to actually try.**
**Result: Valdemar/Sjórseiðr places 2nd in the joust.** Montverte gets the satisfaction of a clean win.

title: Dagmar's dimicatio final — a clean win, then a mirror-match loss to Karis of Oleron
notes: Two-match final. Dagmar means to win outright against a Tytalus opponent (name garbled in the recording) and go easy on Oleron's finalist as a diplomatic courtesy — but the second match, against a Criamon built by the GM as a deliberate mirror of Dagmar's own sheet, turns into a real, hard-fought loss.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — dimicatio final, two matches (vs. the Tytalus magus, then vs. Karis ex Criamon).
body_text:
Dagmar entered the dimicatio final needing to beat two opponents: a **Tytalus magus** first (name unclear in the recording — heard as something close to "Quaerus"), and **Oleron's finalist** second. Going in, Dagmar planned to fight the first for real and **deliberately lose initiative** against Oleron's man as a diplomatic gesture.
**Match 1 — vs. the Tytalus magus.** Dagmar cast **Posing the Silent Question** (Intellego Mentem) again; the opponent fast-cast **Banish the Thought** as a defense, but it backfired — trying to force the intrusive thought out only reinforced it. His shoulders dropped and the match was called for Dagmar. He left the field abruptly, cordial but clearly rattled.
**Match 2 — vs. Karis ex Criamon (Oleron's finalist).** The GM built Karis explicitly as a **mirror of Dagmar's own character sheet** — boyish-faced, younger-looking than his real age, mild and a little blithe in manner.
Karis held his action, then opened with **Pierce the Magical Veil** — attempting to open a regio *on top of his opponent* mid-duel, an unusual and unsettling approach. Followed by **Past Lives**, an eerie effect suggesting the caster's mind holds conversations with great minds of the past (compared at the table to Dante and Virgil), aimed at Dagmar. Dagmar improvised a spontaneous **Intellego/Rego Mentem** defense — grounding himself in "the here, the now, it's me" — and it held (a **personal/momentary/individual** spontaneous effect against a −10 casting-score penalty, needing to clear roughly half the target level).
Karis pressed with **Words of the Unbroken Silence**, trying to plant a message directly in Dagmar's mind — blocked. He then switched tactics entirely and cast **Break the Shield**, a Perdo Vim effect functionally equivalent to dispelling Parma Magica — **Wizard's-War-tier stuff for a tournament match.** It landed. Dagmar described the sensation as the magical equivalent of being about to be disrobed and then not quite. His own spontaneous **Rego Vim** effort to restabilize his Parma (needing 9+, effectively against a −16 penalty) came up **one short**.
**Karis did not follow up.** Dagmar conceded, badly shaken but gracious; Karis, equally gracious: *"You will be delightful competition next tribunal. I look forward to seeing you there."*
**Result: Dagmar/Sjórseiðr places 2nd in the dimicatio** — a real loss to a genuinely tough opponent, not the soft diplomatic throw originally planned, though the outcome (a loss to Oleron) lines up with what Dagmar intended going in.

title: Hastiludium final vs. Lapis Crudus — first place
notes: Lapis Crudus — the recently-freed, 80-year-faerie-imprisoned independent — plays it destructive: fire, a pit trap, and a closing ball of abysmal flame that actually catches the wagon. Grip of Ice and a strong Unseen Porter carry Sjórseiðr across first, unburned. The GM also reveals an earlier bracket round was resolved off-screen in Sjórseiðr's favor to save table time — the covenant wins the Hastiludium outright.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — hastiludium final vs. Lapis Crudus.
body_text:
Opponent: **Lapis Crudus**, the independent covenant recently freed after an 80-year faerie imprisonment, fielding a "premier" Flambeau plus Tremere/Flambeau support (exact roster uncertain even to the GM in the moment). Reputation: destructive and "rollicking" — willing to injure a competitor's mount or rig rather than lose. Riding an enchanted **anvil** in place of a wagon.
Pre-cast as usual: Wizard's Sidestep, Grip of Ice, and a strong **Unseen Porter** pull (an exceptional roll — noticeably "buffer" than the wagon's usual pull).
**Opening.** A pillar of flame appears directly in the wagon's path; Éogan fast-casts a −5-penalized **Mighty Torrent of Water**, rolls **29**, douses it clean.
Dustin lands **Pillum of Fire** on Lapis Crudus's anvil, heating it forge-orange — countered when their caster **Soothes the Raging Flames** right back down.
Lapis Crudus opens **Pit of the Gaping Earth** in the wagon's path; the Unseen Porter routes around it, costing a little time but avoiding the hazard entirely.
Dustin tries **Broom of the Winds** on their rider to knock them loose; they pivot into **Circling Winds of Protection** instead — deflecting the attack, though it also denies them a wind-assisted speed boost.
**Closing move.** Lapis Crudus throws a **Ball of Abysmal Flame** at the wagon. A fast-cast **Creo Aquam** counter (classic counter-magic, matching totals) fails to beat their casting roll; a follow-up spontaneous dousing effect (needing 23+) rolls only **16** and also falls short — the fire catches.
Rather than break off this late in the race, the crew **rides it out**: a Stamina roll holds up, **Grip of Ice**'s literal ice cushions the burn (the grip loosens as it melts, faces get scorched, nothing worse), and one hand quenches the flame while the other holds the line.
The Unseen Porter's speed edge (**+4 net** relative to the opponents) carries Sjórseiðr across the line first — **no injuries**, thanks to the ice.
**GM note:** an earlier hastiludium bracket round the table didn't have time to play out live was resolved off-screen in Sjórseiðr's favor between sessions, to avoid pushing the tournament into a further session.
**Result: Sjórseiðr wins the Hastiludium outright — 1st place.**

title: Tribunal final standings: Sjórseiðr takes first overall, Confluensis takes the "Siege of Shame"
notes: Full placements read aloud at the closing feast. Confluensis's 13th-place finish ("the Siege of Shame," traditionally zero reward per a historical cheating scandal) directly explains the cold reception Dagmar gets minutes later. Sjórseiðr finishes 1st overall with 51 points and 31 pawns of vis.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — full standings readout at the closing feast.
body_text:
As the Redcaps tallied results, the closing feast doubled as the standings ceremony. Placements as announced (covenant names/ordinal titles as heard — a few uncertain):
  • **21st — the "Siege of Alms"** → **Florum** (a leash covenant), 12 pawns instead of zero.
  • **13th — the "Siege of Shame"** → **Confluensis** — **zero pawns**. There's Tribunal-wide lore behind the 13th-place designation, tied to a historical cheating scandal; landing there is a real public humiliation, not just a bad finish.
  • **7th — the "Siege of Notatus"** → **Fudarus**, 17 pawns. (Siege name confirmed against the tribunal workbook's prize-rank table, not the recording itself, which was unclear here.)
  • **4th — Montverte**, 15 pawns.
  • **3rd — Merces Aurea**, 30 points.
  • **2nd — the "Siege of Valor"** → **Oleron**, 31 points.
  • **1st — "The Siege of Normandy"** → **Sjórseiðr**, with a total of **51 points and a reward of 31 pawns of vis** — the second-place gap was 31 to 51, meaning the Hastiludium win alone pulled the covenant well clear of the tie.
A representative from each covenant was called forward in order to draft prizes.

title: First-pick prize draft: Mont-Saint-Michel tide pools, a Terram summa, and Subtle Knives
notes: As tribunal winner, Dagmar leads the pick formally on the covenant's behalf. First vis-source pick and two library picks locked in on the call; remaining picks (20 of 31 prize pawns) to be settled asynchronously with the GM after the session. CORRECTED 2026-06-20 against the tribunal workbook's library list: the session-6 draft had swapped which book was "quality 17" — that was the Aquam summa the party passed on, not the Terram one they actually took.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — prize draft at the closing feast.
body_text:
**Vis-source pick (1st overall pick, uncontested at that slot):** the **Mont-Saint-Michel tide pools** — a high-value, conveniently coastal Aquam source.
**Library picks**, drawn from a partial list the GM shared mid-session and confirmed against the tribunal workbook's library data:
  • **First pick — "De Lapii"**, a rare branch-specific **Terram summa** (Level 17 · Quality 14). Reaction at the table: "that thing's nuts," "I didn't even know books like that existed" — Éogan pushed hardest for this one and it was the clear top priority.
  • **Passed over — "The Primal Power"**, an **Aquam summa** (Level 9 · Quality 17) that came up in the same conversation. High quality, but Éogan's own Aquam score is already **17** — well past the book's level-9 cap — so it would teach him nothing; the party let it go.
  • **Second pick — "Subtle Knives"**, a Penetration summa under Hermetic Theory & Abilities — Éogan's self-described "far second" choice, still locked in for the covenant's library.
**Bookkeeping:** roughly **11 of the covenant's 31 prize pawns** were spent across these first three picks (picks cost one pawn each as the draft cycles through every covenant in placement order); **20 remain** for further rounds, to be resolved asynchronously by the GM after the session as the pick order continues.

title: Bertrand denies the book-storage arrangement ever happened
notes: Fresh off the Siege of Shame, Bertrand flatly denies the morning's negotiation ever happened, then turns back to his meal. The book-storage question is back open — Fudarus or Oleron are the live alternatives, with Oleron the more promising given how Raoul's conversation goes minutes later.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — Dagmar's follow-up with Bertrand after the standings.
body_text:
Confluensis never followed up with terms before the finals ended, as promised. Dagmar sought out **Bertrand ex Verditius** directly at the feast to close the loop.
Bertrand's response, cold and immediate: **"I know of no arrangement."** He turned back to his food without another word.
Dagmar's read leaving the conversation: Confluensis is not housing the books. Given the timing — this lands minutes after Confluensis's public **13th-place humiliation** — the snub reads less like forgetfulness and more like wounded pride refusing to be seen doing a favor for the covenant that just helped bury them.
**Open thread:** the covenant's prize texts still need a custodian. Fudarus (closer, but Dagmar's openly not fond of Tytalus magi) and Oleron (further, but visibly warmer toward Sjórseiðr as of this same feast) are the two live options.

title: Éogan smooths things over with Raoul of Oleron
notes: Éogan apologizes for the covenant's matches not going Oleron's way as intended. Raoul waves it off — genuinely delighted that Sjórseiðr's rise embarrassed Confluensis and Montverte — and starts treating the covenant as a peer, floating a favorable resource swap.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — Éogan's post-standings conversation with Raoul.
body_text:
Éogan sought out **Raoul of Oleron** after the standings to apologize — the covenant had hoped the finals would go Oleron's way as a courtesy, but between real opposition and events moving faster than planned, that didn't fully happen.
Raoul brushed it off immediately, in good humor, and pulled Éogan down for a drink instead: as far as he's concerned, Sjórseiðr beating **Confluensis and Montverte** — old rivals of Oleron's within the tribunal's leash-covenant politics — is a win worth celebrating regardless of who beat whom in the bracket.
**Reading of the room:** Raoul now treats Sjórseiðr as something close to a peer rather than a prospective vassal — "between the two of us, we're running away with it" — and is open to working together where interests align.
**Concrete offer:** Oleron has additional easily-reachable island/coastal resources not on the official prize list that Raoul is willing to trade flexibly for something more inland, further south — convenient if the covenant ends up routing through Oleron territory anyway (e.g. to store Wilhelm's books there instead of Confluensis).

title: Dietrich warns Wilhelm about the company he's keeping
notes: Wilhelm is still processing the covenant's win as a cheerful, low-stakes camp-games victory. Dietrich, working purely off tavern chatter and not the covenant's actual politics, still reads the room correctly enough to pull his brother aside.
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — Dietrich's aside to Wilhelm at the feast.
body_text:
As the covenant's win rippled through the feast, Wilhelm's read on the whole tournament stayed resolutely innocent: to him it landed somewhere between a summer-camp relay race and being crowned king-for-a-day at a village fair — fun, a little silly, not obviously dangerous.
A nearby onlooker (heard as **Helga**) pointedly noted that a lot of covenants seem awfully sore about losing what's ostensibly just a game — more than mere competitive pride, it's described as **a reaffirming of the order of things**, one Sjórseiðr just upended by winning fair and square, with very material seven-year consequences attached (first pick of the tribunal's rare texts and resources).
**Dietrich**, without knowing any of the covenant's actual political entanglements, picked up enough from the ambient chatter to pull Wilhelm aside privately: *"Brother. I think you should be mindful about how deeply you throw your lot in with them. I believe they have made some enemies."* He then stepped back to let Wilhelm keep his privacy with the rest of the table.
Wilhelm, still mentally filing the win as a harmless game, didn't take the warning especially seriously — his more pressing concern stayed retrieving his stolen Latin manuscript and getting to Ireland.

title: Season plans: Ireland, the Isle of Man, and a covenant full of quiet magic items
notes: Travel and season assignments locked in for the trip home. CORRECTED 2026-06-20: the covenant does NOT winter on the Isle of Man this year after all — see session 7, they push on to winter near Carrick, Ireland instead. Running gag: Wilhelm's been sitting on a bottomless grain dish for weeks without mentioning it (quantity also corrected 2026-06-20: six million cubic yards, not one).
source: Transcript 2026-05-23 — closing-session travel/season planning.
body_text:
**Travel.** The **Brineborn** (Éogan's ship) carries Éogan, Wilhelm, Hilda, and one research assistant north toward **Dragon's Rest**, then **Scarem Montem** (to retrieve Wilhelm's stolen Latin thesis copy), then on to **Ireland** for Wilhelm's promised folk-magic fieldwork. Separately, **Valerian**, aboard the **Adamant**, ferries **Dietrich**, Hilda's remaining research assistant, and Wilhelm's other assistant toward a rendezvous at Dragon's Rest.
**Wintering — SUPERSEDED, see session 7 (2026-06-20).** The table's first pass at this had the covenant wintering on the Isle of Man; that was revised one session later to wintering near Carrick, Ireland instead, with the Isle of Man kept only as a waypoint stop (see [053_2026-06-20_ireland-travel-plan-finalized] for the corrected version).
**Autumn season assignments:**
  • **Dagmar** — heading to Oleron with the covenant's prize books; see the dedicated session-7 entry for the expanded plan (he ends up wintering there, not just spending a season).
  • **Dustin** — Learn Teaching from Henri (apprenticeship prerequisite).
  • **Wilhelm** — undecided between Ireland weather-magic fieldwork and a research track reverse-engineering formulaic (ritual) magic's underlying structure by close study of Hermetic ritual, spontaneous, potion, and enchantment sub-systems plus the semi-integrated longevity-ritual and Parma Magica traditions — looking for the shared principle underneath all of it.
  • **Éogan** — developing spells to industrialize dried-fruit and fruit-juice separation as a **non-magical, tradable commodity** for dockside trade, with an eye toward tribunal-to-tribunal arbitrage (some tribunals police magically-produced goods far more strictly than others).
  • **Dustin** — two seasons teaching his apprentice **Stijntje** a minor virtue: **Inventive Genius** in spring, then **Auram** in summer.
  • **Dietrich** — a season getting initiated (through one of the tribunal contacts made this week) into a minor virtue, so he can formally teach the folk-magic system at his Cologne cathedral school starting Fall — needed to satisfy his twice-yearly teaching obligation as a master there.
  • Still unassigned: the recurring **Summer Fog** and **Black Horse of Boulogne** vis-source seasons. Valerian was previously pegged for Summer Fog.
**Running gag.** Wilhelm's graduation research project turns out to be a large stone dish that is **always full of grain** (CORRECTED 2026-06-20: **six million cubic yards'** worth before it would ever run dry, not one — a delay-cast effect that delays by *volume poured out* rather than by time, which the table confirmed is a standard Hermetic ritual effect, not a homebrew "virtual" spell) — magically produced content by any tribunal's reckoning, and thus a genuine arbitrage asset next to the covenant's existing enchanted freshwater barrels. He'd apparently had it out and in casual use for weeks before it occurred to him, entirely without irony, to mention it to his hosts.
